intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: The Fat Goose inn is fast asleep. But every night, strange sounds come from the cellar: rustling, clinking and a little giggle.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: My spoons are gone. So are my buttons, and my best frying pan! Somebody is taking everything that shines.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: Go down and sort it out. But don't smash the barrels. That's my kvass in there.

intro.speaker: hero
intro.text: Well, shall we go down?

variants.warden: Stay behind me. I go first, as always.
variants.wind-archer: Quiet. I hear tiny paws. Lots of tiny paws.
variants.herbalist: Rats? Good thing I packed my bite ointment.
variants.rogue: Cellars are my favorite part of town. After the rooftops.
variants.elementalist: My book says gremlins fear sparks. Let's find out!
variants.tinker: Bolt, sniff around. But don't bite anything rusty.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: Off you go, then. I'll put the kettle on.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The rat squeaked, dropped its spoon and dashed into a crack. The fog drifted off it like smoke.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: In the wine cellar, a gremlin sits on a chest. On his head is Mistress Marta's frying pan, worn like a helmet.

lines.speaker: rogue
lines.text: A frying pan for a helmet? Bold. But I'm taking it back.

lines.speaker: marta
lines.text: Hello down there! I hear banging! I hope that's not my kvass.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: Inside the chest, under a heap of stolen spoons, something began to glow warmly.

victory.speaker: hero
victory.text: It's glowing!

variants.warden: Wow! It glows like a lantern at the fair.
variants.wind-archer: So warm. Like holding a bit of sunshine.
variants.herbalist: It smells of honey and light. A good sign.
variants.elementalist: Incredible! May I hold it? I'll be careful!
variants.tinker: Fine work. Who broke you, poor thing?

victory.speaker: marta
victory.text: That's a piece of our Lantern! Those critters were hoarding it like treasure.

victory.speaker: marta
victory.text: I'll wrap it in a scarf. Something tells me this is only the beginning.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Hello, Bravehearts! Come up from the cellar before the rats take your boots too.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Have a snack, patch yourselves up, and we'll try again.

epilogue.speaker: marta
epilogue.text: The spoons are back, and so is the frying pan. It does have tiny tooth marks now.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Beyond the town begins Thornwood. The fog lies low here, like a cat sneaking up on a mouse.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: The forester saw a light near the old lodge. The same glow as our lantern piece.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: The path is short but prickly. Don't dawdle. Just head for the lodge.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Yellow eyes flash in the bushes. One pair, then another, then one more.

intro.speaker: hero
intro.text: Someone's there!

variants.wind-archer: Movement in the bushes! Two. No, four.
variants.rogue: Shh. Someone's there. And they're not very polite.
variants.elementalist: I feel magic. And I don't like it.
variants.tinker: Bolt is growling. Trouble is close.

lines.speaker: herbalist
lines.text: Thorns don't prick out of spite. Walk around the bushes and they'll leave you alone.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The ravine is narrow and dark. Something iron glints between the rocks. It looks like a trap.

lines.speaker: wind-archer
lines.text: I grew up in the mountains, near wolves. They aren't mean. They're just lost in the fog.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The wolf shook its head as if waking up, and bounded into the woods. Without the fog, it is just a gray wolf again.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A big fellow in a black and purple scarf guards the lodge. A bandit!

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: The lodge was empty. Only ashes from a campfire, boot prints, and a scarf on a nail.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: On the table lay a map. A cross was marked on the old mill by the marsh.

victory.speaker: marta
victory.text: The mill? Good old Bruno the miller lives there. What would bandits want with him?

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Not all at once, Bravehearts. Even wolves don't find the path the first time.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Mend your cloaks, and I'll give you more ointment for the scratches.

epilogue.speaker: marta
epilogue.text: The forester sent a basket of mushrooms. He says the wolves are calm and polite again, just like before.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: The river has burst its banks, and the old mill stands knee-deep in water. The wheel creaks, though nobody turns it.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: Bandits guard the yard. And inside, something mumbles. Something big and wet.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: They say the sluice has a lever that lets the water out. Find it, and things get easier.

intro.speaker: hero
intro.text: We have to help Bruno.

variants.warden: Wet boots are no reason to turn back.
variants.wind-archer: Water hides our steps. Stay close.
variants.herbalist: Bruno always gave me bagels. We have to help him.
variants.rogue: Bandits in someone else's yard? Rude. I always ask permission. Sometimes.
variants.elementalist: So much water! Too bad I haven't learned to dry it up.
variants.tinker: A mill wheel is a machine. And I love rescuing machines.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Bog slimes bubble in the sluice. By the wall stands an old lever, covered in mud.

lines.speaker: tinker
lines.text: The lever is fine, just rusty. Somebody go and give it a good pull!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The wheel creaked and stopped. Slowly, the Bog Miller rises from the water.

lines.speaker: miller
lines.text: Who dared to stop my mill?! Did you come to take the light too?

lines.speaker: miller
lines.text: My head hums like a millstone. Who are you? No, go away! The fog says you are enemies!

lines.speaker: hero
lines.text: Bruno, we're friends! Hang on!

variants.warden: Bruno, we're friends! Hang on, we'll pull you out.
variants.wind-archer: He's fighting the fog. Just a little more!
variants.herbalist: Bruno, it's me, the Herbalist! Remember my herbs and your bagels!
variants.rogue: Uncle Bruno, wake up! You're a good man, I know it.
variants.elementalist: The fog is losing its grip! I can feel it!
variants.tinker: Almost there. This mud will slide right off, like rust off a gear.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: The mud slides off the Miller, and he is himself again: tired, kind Bruno.

victory.speaker: miller
victory.text: Oh, my head is like a millstone. How long was I asleep?

victory.speaker: herbalist
victory.text: Here, Bruno, a sip of mint tea. You'll feel new in an hour.

victory.speaker: miller
victory.text: I remember a tall man in a cloak made of shadow. On his chest hung a glass ball, and inside it was our light.

victory.speaker: miller
victory.text: He called himself Shadowhand. His men hauled crates to the old watchtower.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: That wet giant is still our Bruno, only muddled. Don't give up. He is waiting for you.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Dry your boots by the stove, and back to the mill you go.

epilogue.speaker: marta
epilogue.text: Bruno ate three bowls of soup and fell asleep right at the table. Let him sleep. He earned it.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Lights burn again in the tower above the pass. But this light is cold and purple.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: Bruno says Shadowhand's cultists hid the second piece of the Lantern up there.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: The door to the upper floor is locked. One of the cultists carries the key. Go and find it.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: The runes on the walls flash, one after another. Stone sentinels open their eyes.

intro.speaker: hero
intro.text: They're awake!

variants.warden: Stone sentinels? Let's see which of us guards better.
variants.wind-archer: The wind smells of mountains. Almost like home.
variants.herbalist: I don't like these runes. Stay off the purple tiles.
variants.rogue: A tower, a locked door, and the key in someone else's pocket. Perfect evening.
variants.elementalist: Gloom runes! I saw them in a forbidden book. Well, I almost didn't read it.
variants.tinker: Stone sentinels are ancient automatons. Bolt, don't bark. They're nervous.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Gloom cultists whisper in the barracks. Glowing rune circles surround them on the floor.

lines.speaker: elementalist
lines.text: These runes protect the cultists. Lure them out of the circles!

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The blue spark in the sentinel's eyes went out. The stone is just stone again.

lines.speaker: warden
lines.text: Rest now, stone friend. Your watch is over.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The lock clicked. A shadow slipped up the stairs. Someone is already waiting on the upper floor.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The shadows in the tower grow thicker. Time to grab the light and head for the gate!

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: The second piece of the Lantern is warm, like bread from the oven.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: The two pieces fit together, as if they had always been waiting for each other. But without its heart, the Lantern cannot shine.

victory.speaker: marta
victory.text: And this black glass key opens a cave under the Gray Mountains. The old folks call it the Heart of Gloom.

victory.speaker: wind-archer
victory.text: The Gray Mountains are my home. I know the way.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: The tower is tall and the stairs are steep. Never mind. Next time you'll climb faster.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Just remember: the light must not only be found, but carried home.

epilogue.speaker: marta
epilogue.text: Tomorrow the whole town will see you off. The baker is already kneading bread for the road.

intro.speaker: narrator
intro.text: Under the Gray Mountains, behind a door of black glass, hides the Heart of Gloom.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: Shadowhand keeps our light there. Dark braziers stand along the walls. Light them, and the shadow has nowhere to hide.

intro.speaker: marta
intro.text: And come back, all of you. I'll be counting you at the door.

intro.speaker: hero
intro.text: Let's get our light back.

variants.warden: My shield was once the door of our town hall. Today it guards Alba again.
variants.wind-archer: I know these mountains. It was never this dark here.
variants.herbalist: I packed all my herbs. Even the ones that smell like socks.
variants.rogue: Stealing a whole town's light? Even I wouldn't do that.
variants.elementalist: Fire and wind are with me. Watch out, Shadowhand!
variants.tinker: Bolt, it's going to get dark. Stay close to me.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: The wraith melted away like fog in the sun. The tunnel grew a little brighter.

lines.speaker: shadowhand
lines.text: Did you bring me a little more light? How kind.

lines.speaker: shadowhand
lines.text: The gloom is not evil, little ones. It only waits until all the lights go out.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: Three dark braziers stand along the walls. While they stay unlit, Shadowhand is almost untouchable.

lines.speaker: narrator
lines.text: A crack runs across the glass ball on Shadowhand's chest. Golden rays shine through it.

lines.speaker: shadowhand
lines.text: Enough games! Now I will take your light too!

victory.speaker: shadowhand
victory.text: No! Take this glow away!

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: The ball shattered, and the stolen light burst out of the cave and into the sky.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: Shadowhand crumbled into a swarm of black butterflies, and they fluttered away into the dark.

victory.speaker: narrator
victory.text: Above the town hall, the Guardian Lantern shone again. The fog retreated all the way to the edge of the forest.

victory.speaker: hero
victory.text: We did it!

variants.rogue: Easy. Next time, make it harder, please.
variants.elementalist: Did you see that? Did you see that fire?!

victory.speaker: marta
victory.text: The Braveheart Guild lives again. And I'll embroider your names on the banner myself.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Hello, Bravehearts! The fog won't take you. Come back, and we'll try again.

defeat.speaker: marta
defeat.text: Shadowhand is strong, but the braziers are stronger. Light all three, and he can't hide.

epilogue.speaker: marta
epilogue.text: Get some rest. They say something goes bump in the Gray Mountains at night.
